description:
Turbine (crates/tampines/src/components/turbine.rs:13) has exactly two fields -- inlet: HemSteamCv and adiabatic_efficiency: Ratio. Zero geometry.

Part of op-dt3.17. The digital-twin widget layer must derive a component's on-screen size from its REAL dimensions; the engine crate forbids new physics, so the dimension must exist here in tampines.

DO NOT use HemSteamCv::get_volume() as a size -- it is the thermodynamic control volume, caller-supplied and unvalidated, conventionally a 1 m3 dummy (get_ref_vol() returns exactly 1.0 m3). It describes the fluid parcel, not the machine.

Prefer explicit named dimensions where shape matters to the drawing; a single nominal Volume is acceptable where only a rough size correlation is wanted. Document units and valid ranges in the doc comment per the workspace human-interface rule, and keep uom types.

Maintainer's steer (2026-08-03): a rough size correlation with respect to volume is enough for a turbine; too much detail may confuse the end user.
title: tampines Turbine: add casing/envelope dimensions

design:
Child epic of the nuclear refinery programme (bn op-upme).

**Fidelity target: Crude estimate initially**

Hydrotreating and hydrocracking produce H2S and NH3, which must be separated
before H2 recycle.

```
H2-rich recycle gas -> acid-gas removal -> sweet H2 recycle
                                        -> H2S-rich acid gas -> SRU
```

**Audit upstream DWSIM absorber/stripper capabilities before implementing a new
amine unit.** The crate already has `columns/` (15 files) and
`thermo/electrolyte.rs`, `thermo/electrolyte_svle.rs`, `thermo/sour_water.rs`
-- an amine or sour-water path may be closer than it appears.

Initial steady-state AGR **may be equilibrium/efficiency based** if rigorous
electrolyte chemistry is not yet available. **Preserve H2/H2S/NH3/H2O
balances.**

Gates the SRU and the H2 recycle loop.

## Out of scope for this pass (programme-wide)

Do not: port DWSIM UI or graphical flowsheet objects; port CAPE-OPEN unless a
concrete backend requirement exists; reproduce .NET class architecture; make
DWSIM depend on Outram-FOAM; solve thousands of molecular species in the CDU;
implement molecular reconstruction before assay/pseudocomponent CDU works; call
a converged model validated without reference evidence; hide conservation
errors; push to `main`.
title: Refinery: Acid-gas removal

description: GitHub issue #30 comment 2026-08-25: 'To scroll thru the pdfs in continuous mode' -- an Okular-style continuous page-flow view instead of one-page-at-a-time. Pages stack vertically, scrollable as one document; per-page full-res textures rasterized lazily (only pages intersecting the viewport), page size for layout purposes derived cheaply from the existing thumbnail-DPI cache (avoids adding a new page-size-only API call). Toggleable against the existing single-page mode; draw-box/select-text/annotation interactions stay single-page-mode-only for this pass (documented scope cut) -- continuous mode is a reading view.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Implemented. crates/kovan/src/digitiser/gui/desktop/pdf_reader.rs:
- New "Continuous scroll" toggle (default ON per the explicit ask), checkbox in the toolbar.
- `continuous_pages_ui`: all pages stacked vertically in one scrollable canvas. Layout size per page comes cheaply from the already-cached thumbnail texture (op-0y4k) scaled from THUMBNAIL_DPI up to RENDER_DPI, avoiding a full rasterization just to learn dimensions. Actual full-res textures (`full_res_texture`, cached in a new `page_textures` map) are only rasterized for pages intersecting the viewport -- off-screen pages get a placeholder rect, so opening a long document stays cheap.
- Existing saved annotations are shown read-only as an overlay in continuous mode.
- `page_index` auto-tracks whichever page has the most viewport overlap each frame, so the toolbar's "page N/M" readout and single-page mode (if toggled back) stay in sync with scroll position.
- Thumbnail-strip clicks now work correctly in continuous mode too: a new `scroll_to_page` field, consumed via egui's `scroll_to_rect`, jumps the continuous view to the clicked page (previously would have just been silently overwritten by the per-frame visible-page tracking).

Deliberate scope cut, documented in the code: continuous mode is VIEW-ONLY -- draw-box/select-text/annotation *creation* tools stay single-page-mode-only. Re-deriving "which page, and where on it" a click/drag landed across a whole scrolling flow is materially more work than the single-page coordinate math the tools already use, and the ask here was about reading, not digitising.

cargo check --all-targets clean (native + aarch64-linux-android). cargo test --release: 204 kovan lib tests passing. Not committed yet.

title: kovan-gui: PDF reader continuous-scroll mode (view all pages in one flow)
